That is about 13.1% of the 147,782,141 shares outstanding at 2026-09-24 (DEF 14A, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1731348/000114036126037827/ny20076749x2_def14a.htm). findings.finding: On 2026-09-29, Tilray's CEO said BrewDog sales fell as much as 20% year on year after the March takeover, that the numbers were 'horrible', and that sales are still below last year. Tilray has put about $50-60m into stabilising the business. The deal case was $200m annual revenue and about $8m EBITDA, and the July call called BrewDog 'margin accretive'.
findings.question: Q3
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BrewDog was first reported in Q4 FY26 (2026-07-28): beverage +61% with $51.1m from BrewDog, and the stock moved -0.99% on the print. There is no history of the stock reacting to a BrewDog miss.
findings.why_not_priced: No estimate revision after the remark could be found (consensus revenue still implies about $55m of BrewDog in the quarter), and the stock only fell 4.3% over the following five sessions. Caveat that shrinks it: Q4 BrewDog revenue ($51.1m over Mar 2-May 31) already annualised at the $200m plan while it was in the slump, so the plan was set on the depressed base. The surprise is mostly in profit and commentary, not revenue. BrewDog is about 20% of group revenue, and the rest of the company has to carry the quarter.
findings.independence: Same remarks reported independently by thecaterer.com (2026-09-30, https://www.thecaterer.com/news/new-brewdog-owners-plough-50m-into-business-repositioning), where Simon said 'right now we are really seeing strong numbers'. That partly offsets the finding. Both articles rest on the same event.

findings.finding: Fresh peer and market data after Tilray's July call show international medical-cannabis price compression getting worse. On 2026-08-05 Aurora reported international medical revenue +17% (Apr-Jun) while adjusted EBITDA fell from C$10.8m to C$3.4m. German pharmacy flower prices are near EUR 4/g in Q2 2026, and German imports fell in Q1 2026 for the first time in two years.
findings.question: Q4
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q4 FY26 international revenue was +34% with about $21m of price compression flagged, cannabis gross margin held near 40-44%, and the stock moved -0.99%. No clean reaction to this line is on record.
findings.why_not_priced: Slow data the market underweights: a peer's margin collapse and pharmacy price indices move a little each month, and no TLRY estimate revision tied to them could be found. Caveats: this is a proxy (peer, not company), Tilray's international growth includes the April 2026 Lyphe acquisition, and international is under 10% of group revenue. Net of the rest, it stays small.
findings.independence: https://businessofcannabis.com/public-data-is-no-longer-enough-to-understand-the-german-medical-cannabis-market (2026-06-09): German Q1 2026 imports fell and average price per gram is down almost a third since early 2025. This is a different source from Aurora.

findings.finding: Three executives bought stock on the open market during the quarter being reported: the CFO bought 10,000 shares at $4.62 on 2026-08-04, the CSO 2,500 at $4.78 on 2026-08-03 and the General Counsel 2,500 at $4.43 on 2026-08-06. These were with two of the quarter's three months already booked.
findings.why_not_priced: The amounts are small (about $70k in total) and the Form 4s are public, so this is a lead and not a decisive number. A CFO buying in the quarter he is about to report is mild evidence that Q1 does not hold a negative surprise he could see.
findings.independence: The CSO purchase is in a separate filing (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1731348/000117184326005173/ownership.xml); both are insider decisions of the same kind.

outside_window.finding: Broader federal rescheduling of all marijuana to Schedule III is pending the ALJ's recommendation and the DEA Administrator's decision after final briefs on 2026-08-17. There is no deadline, so the timing is unknowable and nothing is dated inside the window.
The 5.20% convertible notes due 2027-06-15 have about $52m of principal left after $18m of exchanges since the 10-K, and the debt-for-equity exchanges continue.

key_questions.answer: Probably at or slightly above the about $12m implied run-rate, guide reiterated. Gross-profit rebuild against Q1 FY26: cannabis gross margin was depressed at 36% then and ran 40-44% in Q4 FY26, worth +$3-5m; distribution margin 11% to 13-14%, +$2m; legacy beer gross profit -$4-5m; BrewDog adds gross profit but also bar and marketing opex, EBITDA about 0 to +$2m; Project 420 savings. That gives about $10-16m. The fresh peer evidence on international pricing (Aurora) argues against the full cannabis margin recovery, so the centre is about $12-13m, which is not a usable gap. All inputs predate the July call except the peer data and the CEO's BrewDog remarks, and both of those lean negative. Insider open-market buying in August is a mild positive filed separately.

investment_decision.reason: Q1 (revenue) and Q5 (dilution) came back at answers the market quantitatively holds: consensus revenue matches my segment rebuild, and the share count is public. Q2 (EBITDA/guide) has no quantified consensus, but my own rebuild lands on the guide-implied run-rate and gives no gap. Q3 and Q4 carry small, partly proxied negatives that a 13% short base offsets, so impact_sum of -0.4 is too small to carry a position, and no_trade agrees with its near-zero sign.
investment_decision.what_would_change_it: A cut to the FY27 $68-75m EBITDA guide, or a Q1 EBITDA well below $10m (short), against a reaffirmed guide with Q1 EBITDA at or above $15m (long, squeeze risk).
